title: Orbital-Selective Spin Splitting in the Altermagnetic Ti$_2$XX' Monolayers
abstract: Altermagnets have attracted intensive attention recently, owing to their unique combination of zero net magnetic moment of antiferromagnets and momentum space spin-splitting of ferromagnets. Herein, we systematically explore monolayer altermagnetic Ti$_2$XX' (X/X' = F, Cl, Br, I) materials for novel electronic properties. Especifically, spin-splitting exists in the valence bands of all studied materials, whereas several compositions exhibit nearly spin-degenerate conduction bands near the Fermi level, which is markedly different from conventional altermagnets. This phenomenon can be attributed to the bond-angle-sensitive super-exchange occurring in the $d_{xz}$ or $d_{yz}$ orbitals, while the super-exchange of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital is not sensitive to the Ti-X-Ti bond angle. Motivated by this intriguing phenomenon, Fermi level modulation via doping or heterostructure construction enables the transition between two electronic states, endowing these materials great application potential in information storage devices.
summary: This work investigates the electronic structure of monolayer altermagnetic Ti2XX' materials, finding unique spin-splitting patterns. The key finding is the presence of nearly spin-degenerate conduction bands, which are sensitive to the Ti-X-Ti bond angle. This tunability suggests these materials are promising candidates for next-generation spintronic and information storage devices.
main_problem: To systematically explore the novel electronic properties, particularly the transition between spin-degenerate and spin-split states, in monolayer altermagnetic Ti2XX' materials.
main_result: The materials exhibit anomalous nearly spin-degenerate conduction bands near the Fermi level, which can be tuned by doping or heterostructure construction, suggesting potential for information storage devices.
method: First-principles calculations using DFT (PBE and HSE06 functionals) combined with tight-binding models and spin-resolved conductivity simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the monolayer altermagnetic Ti2XX' (X/X' = F, Cl, Br, I). The analysis focuses on the interplay between bond-angle-sensitive super-exchange interactions in the d_xz/d_yz orbitals.
key_observables: Spin-splitting magnitude ($\Delta E$), spin-resolved conductivities ($\sigma_{xx}^{\uparrow}, \sigma_{xx}^{\downarrow}$), and the degree of spin degeneracy in the conduction bands.
important_parameters: Ti-X-Ti bond angle ($	heta$), Fermi level position, and the choice of DFT functional (PBE vs. HSE06).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ligand-mediated super-exchange picture and uses the Slater-Koster two-center approximation in the tight-binding model.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic structures, band-structure results confirming spin-split valence bands and spin-degenerate conduction bands, and projected band weight curves illustrating orbital contributions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the unique spin-splitting features in the valence bands to explaining the anomalous conduction band degeneracy via bond-angle-sensitive super-exchange, culminating in the potential for electronic state switching via doping.
why_interesting: The study of orbital-selective spin splitting and the ability to tune electronic states via structural parameters (bond angle) touches upon emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter that are relevant to advanced quantum materials design.
